strings.name: Olafur Eliasson
strings.role: Artist · Perception, natural phenomena and climate
strings.summary: Raised in Iceland and Denmark, Eliasson works with light, water, mist, mirrors and temperature to make viewers aware of how they perceive their surroundings. The weather project created a shared artificial climate inside a museum; The New York City Waterfalls and Ice Watch entered public spaces. Collaborations with architects, engineers and scientists connect art with energy and ecology, emphasizing bodily participation and changing viewpoints.
strings.coverageNote: Research cutoff: 2026-11-13. Selected milestones span 1967–2026; this is not a complete catalogue or live news archive.
strings.influence.rationale: Explored perception and the environment through light, water and spatial installations, connecting contemporary art with climate issues and experiences of public space.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace and upbringing
strings.facts.fact-01.value: Born in Copenhagen, Denmark; raised in Iceland and Denmark
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Royal Danish Academy of Fine Arts, 1989–1995
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: Natural phenomena experienced together
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: The weather project used an artificial sun, mist and mirrors to make the museum and visitors’ bodies part of a shared experience.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: Environmental questions in public space
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: Ice Watch and Little Sun create different ways to encounter glacial melting, climate and access to energy.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: ARoS announces a long-term collaboration
strings.timeline.event-01.text: The museum and studio announced Shared Futures, with Thin Ice planned for autumn 2027. This records an announcement, not a completed exhibition.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Your curious journey reaches Manila
strings.timeline.event-02.text: The MCAD exhibition surveyed three decades of light, water and environmental phenomena, remaining on view beyond the research cutoff.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Presents Ice Watch for the first time
strings.timeline.event-03.text: With geologist Minik Rosing, he brought Greenland ice to a Copenhagen square, making melting an accessible climate experience.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Co-founds Little Sun
strings.timeline.event-04.text: With engineer Frederik Ottesen, he developed solar lights and energy projects connecting design with the needs of off-grid communities.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Your rainbow panorama opens
strings.timeline.event-05.text: A circular colored-glass walkway on ARoS’s roof transforms views of Aarhus as visitors move.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Installs The New York City Waterfalls
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Temporary artificial waterfalls connected flowing water, infrastructure and urban perception, expanding encounters with contemporary art.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Presents The weather project at Tate Modern
strings.timeline.event-07.text: An artificial sun and mist transformed the Turbine Hall into a shared experience of a constructed natural environment.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Establishes his Berlin studio
strings.timeline.event-08.text: After completing art studies he moved to Berlin, bringing spatial research, technical experiments and artistic production into an interdisciplinary studio.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Enters the Royal Danish Academy
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Studies continuing until 1995 supported his developing interest in how light, space and natural phenomena are perceived.
strings.timeline.event-10.title: Born in Copenhagen
strings.timeline.event-10.text: Born in Denmark and raised between Iceland and Denmark; both natural and social environments became contexts for his work.
